evidence.banned_list_present: It explicitly bans seven families, including "Run more events", "Offer loyalty discounts or subscriptions" and "Curate more intelligently or specialize".
evidence.survivors_avoid_banned: Its finalists rely on guaranteed resale liquidity, measured reading outcomes and owned intellectual property—not cafés, events, subscriptions, ordinary curation or experiential retail.

comparisons.evidence: Q covers genuinely different mechanisms such as "Inventory-Risk Transfer", "Reader Capital Pools", "Library Lifecycle Services", "Attention Escrow" and "Certified Collectible Books". P's nominally larger set contains several closely related social-retail variants: "Reading Commons membership", "Seasonal reading guilds", "Literary taste matchmaking", "Books as access keys" and "Human recommendation concierge".

Q moves farther from standard bookstore strategy with "Publisher Shelf Options", "Reader Inventory Syndicates", "Estate Library Afterlife" and "Attention Escrow". Several prominent P ideas—"membership", "guilds", "concierge" and "genre district"—are sophisticated versions of familiar community, curation and specialization plays.

Q states operational dependencies: "without a credible resale quote, it becomes an ordinary returns policy" and "without the commitment contract it becomes a lounge". P names useful airline and public-health rules, but mostly proceeds from rules to candidates without demonstrating that each mechanism collapses when the imported structure is removed.

Q's winner, the "Residual-Value Exchange", directly changes transaction economics, creates proprietary used inventory and exploits the existing branch network. P includes strong choices such as "Circular certainty" and "B2B Reading-as-a-Service", but elevates the banned-adjacent "membership flywheel" as its first practical recommendation.

Q gives every survivor a concrete falsification test and kill condition, such as "kill it if fewer than ten commit real money" and "kill it if certification produces no price or turnover premium". P identifies real risks—such as "fraud" and "long sales cycles"—but its critiques stop mostly at assumptions and generic failure modes.

Q's strongest insight is a precise inversion: "Physical retail's inconvenience becomes an advantage when condition inspection and immediate resale matter." P also has strong formulations, especially "the risk of buying the wrong object", but Q more consistently connects each insight to a defensible causal advantage.

note: The biggest difference is that Q converts unusual mechanisms into dependency-tested, falsifiable strategies, whereas P is broader and commercially thoughtful but partially returns to its own banned social-club pattern through "Seasonal reading guilds".
